sentences: A primitive word cannot be obtained by repeating a shorter word two or more times.
The project asks whether the collection of all primitive words over an alphabet with at least two letters is non-context-free.
This tests whether a context-free grammar can describe the absence of every possible global repetition pattern.
Ruling out narrower grammar classes does not rule out arbitrary context-free grammars, which may exploit ambiguous derivations.
The question connects elementary word periodicity with the expressive limits of recursive language descriptions.
